sources.title: RIT NUTR-550 Community Nutrition course description
sources.author: Rochester Institute of Technology
sources.content: NUTR-550 studies current nutrition issues and the delivery of food and nutrition services in communities. The course is designed to develop skills needed to deliver services in public-health and private-sector settings.

sources.title: Community Planning for Health Assessment and Improvement Planning
sources.author: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.content: A community health assessment develops a comprehensive picture of health status, contributing factors, higher-risk groups, and community resources through systematic collection and analysis of multiple data sources. CDC describes broad community engagement, multisector collaboration, transparency, evidence-based interventions, attention to disparities, and continuous evaluation as important principles. A community health improvement plan uses assessment results to define measurable objectives, coordinated strategies, accountable entities, and shared ownership.

sources.title: CDC Program Evaluation Framework, 2024
sources.author: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.content: The CDC framework contains three cross-cutting actions: engage collaboratively, promote fair and just evaluation practices and outcomes, and learn from and use insights. Its five standards are relevance and utility, rigor, independence and objectivity, transparency, and ethics. Its six iterative steps are assess context, describe the program, focus evaluation questions and design, gather credible evidence, generate and support conclusions, and act on findings.

sources.title: SNAP-Ed Evaluation Framework and Interpretive Guide
sources.author: U.S. Department of Agriculture, Food and Nutrition Service
sources.content: The SNAP-Ed framework organizes nutrition and physical-activity indicators across short-term readiness and goals, medium-term behavioral or environmental changes, long-term maintenance, and population results. It includes individual, environmental-setting, and sector levels so a program can distinguish immediate participation from sustained behavior and broader conditions.

sources.title: The National Cancer Institute Dietary Assessment Primer
sources.author: Frances E. Thompson and colleagues
sources.content: The Dietary Assessment Primer profiles 24-hour recalls, food records, food-frequency questionnaires, and screeners and recommends choosing an approach according to the research objective. Self-report instruments contain measurement error. Random error adds variability, while systematic error can bias estimates. Multiple instruments, repeat measures, or reference biomarkers can sometimes address different weaknesses, but method choice and interpretation must reflect the error structure.
